messages.content:
<question>
In the lease es-lease-02, a Valencia flat let by a company, clause 2 sets a three-year term that ends without extension and has the tenant waive the extensions of art. 9, and clause 6 updates the deposit (fianza) every year. Are those clauses valid under Spanish law on the signing date?
</question>

<answer>
No. When the landlord is a legal person, a lease shorter than seven years is extended obligatorily by yearly periods until it reaches seven years, unless the tenant gives 30 days' notice of not renewing [1]. A three-year term therefore cannot end without extension against the tenant's wish [1].

During the first five years of the contract, or the first seven years if the landlord is a legal person, the deposit is not subject to updating [2]. Updating the deposit every year is therefore not allowed [2].
</answer>

<reference>
No. When the landlord is a legal person, a lease shorter than seven years is extended obligatorily by yearly periods until it reaches seven years, unless the tenant gives 30 days' notice of not renewing (art. 9.1 of the Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos), so a three-year term cannot end without extension against the tenant's wish. During the first five years of the contract, or the first seven if the landlord is a legal person, the deposit is not subject to updating, so updating it every year is not allowed (art. 36.2).
</reference>
